maria: Heads-up — I'm sketching a plan to extract common routing + telemetry into a lightweight 'chorus' sidecar. The goal is reducing duplicated hotpath logic across our model-serving slices without opening a huge latency tax.
aj: Nice. quick question — where's the critical path? what's the expected latency impact?
sam: We should avoid extra blocking RPCs. Prefer an in-proc shim for hotpath ops and sidecar for async telemetry.
maria: Agreed. Current idea: chorus = small runtime shim + sidecar. Shim hooks into request path for routing hints and lightweight guards; sidecar handles async exports, observability, and policy decisions. Legacy services fall back to in-process behavior.
elaine: Who owns chorus? infra or runtime? Ownership matters for deploy cadence and SLA.
maria: Proposal: infra owns deployment/scale/OS; runtime owns API contract and kernel compatibility. We'll codify SLOs and WG owners.
aj: Also propose hard budget: if chorus adds >2ms p99 on a typical hotpath we rollback. We need clear gates.
sam: Migration constraints: kv-cache can't be naively centralized because of sequence affinity. Chorus can provide cache indices/metadata but not be the authoritative hot KV unless proven.
maria: Exactly — plan keeps kv local. Chorus will export cache hints (namespace, prefix fingerprints), which services can optionally use for coordinated caching.
elaine: Compliance note — Chorus must not exfil plaintext inputs for regulated tenants. Need a local-only mode and tenant-level opt-out.
infra-bot: Deploy checklist created: https://gist.mock/chrous-deploy-plan — build image, perf bench, chaos tests, 5% canary x24h, metrics smoke.
maria: Rollout steps (sketch):
```
0: spike — prototype shim + sidecar, perf harness
1: limited canary (5%) with feature-flag gating
2: gradual traffic shift (5 -> 25 -> 75) with burn windows
3: cutover + cleanup + kill-switch retention for 72h
```
aj: I'll own canary metrics and rollback automation. Need to define exact metric thresholds (p50/p95/p99, token-cost delta, error-rate).
sam: I'll own the perf harness — synthetic workload ~10k reqs/s mix, measure tail lat and CPU. Also add token-loss / truncation checks.
elaine: I'll draft privacy checklist and tenant opt-out flow. Also a list of tenants that require local-only.
maria: Risks called out: added indirection might increase SLO noise; ownership/operational blast radius; migration of legacy adapters. Mitigations: feature flags, per-route rollouts, strict perf gates.
aj: Also list of follow-ups: tests for degraded sidecar (how do we degrade gracefully), cost-model impact, and on-call runbook updates.
infra-bot: Chaos tests scheduled on perf cluster for next Tue.
maria: Ok — decision: run spike next week. Action items assigned in thread. :rocket:
aj: LGTM.
sam: I'll start the harness and post preliminary numbers here.
elaine: Adding privacy doc PR after spike.
maria: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for action items and early numbers.
